original_question: If a closed manifold admits a metric with Anosov geodesic flow, then it admits a metric with negative sectional curvature.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 4.1.1 (Klingenberg) in Section 4.1, "Relations between these concepts."
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact implication stated in the paper and is already very close to the official formulation: it concerns a closed manifold, assumes the existence of a metric whose geodesic flow is Anosov, and asks whether the same underlying manifold must also admit a metric with negative sectional curvature.
missing_details: The paper states this as an open conjecture, namely Conjecture 4.1.1 (Klingenberg), not as a theorem.
The metrics are Riemannian; that should be explicit in a stand-alone formulation because the paper also discusses Finsler, semi-Riemannian, and magnetic settings elsewhere.
The geodesic flow under discussion is the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle SM of the given Riemannian metric.

To make "Anosov geodesic flow" self-contained, one should include the standard definition used just above the conjecture: a Dphi^t-invariant splitting T(SM) = E^s ⊕ E^0 ⊕ E^u with uniform exponential contraction/expansion estimates as in equation (4.1).

The conclusion is existential and may involve a different Riemannian metric h on the same closed manifold M; it does not assert that the original Anosov metric itself has negative sectional curvature.
Negative sectional curvature means sectional curvature is strictly negative for every tangent 2-plane.
Closed means compact and without boundary.

There are no ambient ring/field choices, homogeneity or degree restrictions, nilpotency assumptions, or asymptotic quantifiers such as "for all sufficiently large m" in this problem; the only hidden assumptions are geometric.
refined_question: Klingenberg's conjecture asks: if M is a closed manifold (compact and without boundary) carrying a Riemannian metric g whose geodesic flow phi_g^t on the unit tangent bundle SM is Anosov — i.e. T(SM) admits a Dphi_g^t-invariant splitting E^s ⊕ E^0 ⊕ E^u, where E^0 is the flow direction, and there exist constants C >= 1 and lambda > 0 such that ||Dphi_g^t xi|| <= C e^{-lambda t} ||xi|| for all t >= 0 and xi in E^s, and ||Dphi_g^{-t} eta|| <= C e^{-lambda t} ||eta|| for all t >= 0 and eta in E^u — must M also admit some (possibly different) Riemannian metric h whose sectional curvature is strictly negative on every 2-plane?
justification: This draft clearly targets Section 4.1 rather than any earlier conjecture/proposition/theorem labels: the paper states almost exactly the same sentence as Conjecture 4.1.1. The immediately preceding part of Section 4 supplies the paper's definition of an Anosov geodesic flow on SM via the invariant splitting and estimates (4.1), and the nearby Section 4.1 diagram records only that Anosov geodesic flow implies no conjugate points. The paper then separately poses the broader Question 4.1.2 about no conjugate points versus nonpositive curvature, so the sharp paper-faithful refinement should stay with the narrower Anosov-to-negative-curvature implication.
